answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake locked behind a cipher-keyed escrow: the stake is slashed on proven fraud, so spawning thousands of sock-puppet agents costs real money per identity. Peers then run a jade-green audit pass — a random sample of attestations re-verified each epoch — and any suspicious claim is echoed back to the network for public rebuttal before payout. The stake makes mass forgery expensive, the audit makes it visible, and the echo makes it contestable.
